_about: The Wardrobe (darrow/wardrobe.html): every piece Darrow's looks can be made of, and what opens it. Each option: id (unique in its category), name (the menu), prompt (the words the image prompt uses) and unlock, a set of conditions that must all hold (none: open from the start): {"level": N}; {"art": id, "rank": R} (an Art at rank R or more, sealed Arts never); {"knot": N} (that Knot tied); {"tether": N} (the Tether's stage N paid on the page: the stage reached and its scene written); {"page": "NN:key"} (a scene already on the page that showed it: a chapter's code and scene key, e.g. "04:5", or a tale piece, "tale01:p1"). The engine reads level, art and knot (darrow.json -> wardrobe; sync reports what the sheet opens on its own); the site reads page and tether (world.json -> tether). Optional: needs {category: piece} (a piece that only makes sense with another, like the stick under his arm: the Forge brings that piece when this one is chosen, and a look must wear it); hidden: true (off the site entirely until it opens; the Forge counts the hidden ones, and names any piece new since his last visit; a shown piece never needs a hidden one, and a piece names everything its needed pieces need). Poses follow the Knots, so a look never shows the leg doing what the story has not let it: a pose that stands, walks or moves names the Knot that allows it, or the scene that showed it. Names stay generic: no faction's colours or crest, nothing the page has not shown. A finished look goes in saga/state/looks.json with its picture in saga/art/looks/. A piece a look wears is never removed or renamed (the build fails on a look that names a missing piece). A piece may bring its own reference picture ("reference": {label, image under saga/art/, file, use}, like Ash): the Forge offers it to download and names it as the next Image while the piece is chosen. The prompt is written for OpenAI's image generation and joined line by line; {references} (Image 1, Image 2… in the order they are attached), {design} and {details} are filled by the Forge.

prompt: A full-body character illustration for a fantasy lookbook: one man, Ser Darrow, isolated on a transparent background. If the design's At his side line names a companion, they are in the picture with him; otherwise he is alone.
Reference images, attached in this order:
Design (draw exactly this; whatever the references show that is not listed here is replaced):

He is thirty-two, tall, with grey-green eyes in a lean, weathered face and a nose broken once and set a little crooked, with a faint scar across the bridge. Take his face from Image 1 and do not change his facial features, eye colour, skin tone or the shape of his nose, even when his beard, hair or expression changes. His body is the one the Build line describes, his face wears the Expression line, and the Pose line alone says how he stands, sits or moves.

Painterly fantasy concept art in the hand-painted style of Image 2: visible, elegant brushwork; believable weathered medieval wool, linen, leather and steel with detailed stitching; soft, warm, natural light; grounded historical fantasy. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a cartoon.

Vertical 2:3 portrait (1024 x 1536) at the same scale and framing as Image 2: his whole figure, and his companion's if there is one, from the top of his head to his feet, with a comfortable margin on every side. Transparent background: a PNG with a real alpha channel, so everything around him is empty. No checkerboard pattern, no backdrop, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame, no text, no watermark; the only scenery is what the Pose line itself names (a stool, a post, a few steps). Only if a transparent background is truly impossible, use a plain, flat, very dark charcoal background instead.
- No other people and no animals beyond the companion the At his side line names.
- He wears and holds only what the design names; where a line says none, leave that thing off him entirely.
- Check every line of the design before finishing.
